headline: Australian balanced super options returned an estimated 9.1% for FY2026, driven primarily by international shares outperforming domestic equities.
reasoning: Kirby Rappell from SuperRatings noted that balanced superannuation options delivered approximately 9.1% for the financial year, marking a fourth consecutive year of strong returns. The dominant driver was international shares, which significantly outpaced domestic equities. Infrastructure and private equity returns were more muted by comparison. The ASX 200 returned only around 3% (or 6% including dividends) for the year, reflecting the absence of concentrated AI and technology thematics that drove offshore markets.
quote: I think the story has mirrored the last couple of years around in international shares. So if you're on the freight train that has been international shares, you're in a pretty happy spot. And I think it's also causing some pause for some super funds where we'd seen them really enamored with infrastructure and private equity. That's probably a bit more muted. But international shares have won out this year.
episode_title: Patience is your super's superpower| the advisory

headline: Rappell flags a pullback in international shares as the key risk to super returns over the next 12 months, with a 7.3% long-run average as a realistic baseline.
reasoning: Rappell identified the main risk to super returns as international shares failing to maintain their recent momentum. If global equities pull back, it will weigh on balanced option returns given how dominant that asset class has been. He contextualised expectations by noting that since 1992 the long-run average return has been 7.3%, suggesting anything in that range next year would be a solid outcome and outperformance should be treated as a bonus.
quote: I think the main risk is that we don't see, uh, international shares continuing to pick up the slack. Um, if we see that coming off at all, obviously, just like you've seen today in Australian market, some IPOs in the US market really helping to drive that. If that starts to pull back it's going to weigh a bit on return. So I think that's probably the first thing to call out. Secondly, if I look back to 1992 average returns 7.3% looking pretty good. So if we can get another 7.3 for next year, we'll be pretty happy.
episode_title: Patience is your super's superpower| the advisory

headline: AI and technology concentration in global markets explains the wide gap between international and Australian share returns in FY2026.
reasoning: Rappell attributed the significant outperformance of international shares versus Australian equities to the concentrated rally in technology and AI-related names globally. He acknowledged that optimism around AI could eventually flow through to other sectors including mining and infrastructure within the local economy, but for now the gap reflects the lack of equivalent tech exposure on the ASX.
quote: I think very much has been that case of where's technology and where's AI going. And a lot of optimism going through that. And obviously that will flow through to other areas of the economy, hopefully through mining, through infrastructure within the more local economy. But I think it's been a case of, uh, very much that focus on that concentrated number of tech names.
episode_title: Patience is your super's superpower| the advisory

headline: Staying invested rather than timing markets has been the winning strategy for super fund members, with returns of ~13.5% since the start of the Trump presidency despite significant volatility.
reasoning: Rappell emphasised that over 20 to 30 years of superannuation history, attempting to time the market has consistently been a poor strategy. He noted that despite geopolitical noise including the Middle East conflict and Trump-era policy uncertainty, members who stayed invested in balanced options earned approximately 13.5% since the beginning of the Trump presidency. The lesson is that short-term noise should not drive long-term investment decisions.
quote: I think it's it's increasingly clear over the past 20, even 30 years through super trying to time the markets is a nightmare. And it's really hard. I think we're all getting used to uncertainty and volatility. Again. That's making it harder for people to um block out that short term noise. But staying invested has been the order for the day if we look. Ever since the start of the Trump presidency, it's about 13.5% return. Now, despite all the noise that we've been hearing over that period.
episode_title: Patience is your super's superpower| the advisory
